editorial:
Imagine feeling like you failed at your biggest dream. That is exactly where you find Jake, a struggling artist who is finally giving up on New York City and heading back to Ohio. But before he leaves, he gathers his three best buds—Billy, Rocks, and Gunderson—for one last ride. Instead of a car, they decide to walk the entire length of Manhattan. It is a classic setup about friendship and the fear of growing up, giving off a very relaxed, indie vibe that makes you feel like you are just hanging out with the group.

What really works here is the chemistry between the four leads. Their banter feels real, and the pacing keeps you moving right along with them. While some parts of the story feel a bit slow, the emotional payoffs make it worth it. If you love movies about friendship and second chances, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: As the walk ends, Jake finally stops pretending that he has it all figured out. He admits he is scared of the future and tired of lying to himself about his art. The group realizes that moving home is not a failure, but a fresh start. They part ways with a deeper bond, and Jake leaves New York feeling at peace instead of defeated. It wraps up as a sweet reminder that friendship matters more than success.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and buddy comedies.
